title: Terms on Which Money Is Taken in Advance and Held at Collection
content:
A rate class that requires prepayment takes its prepayment share of the whole rental total at the moment
the supplier confirms; a class that does not takes nothing until the counter. This is the basis on which a
Car Rental Rate Classes booking is paid for before the vehicle is collected.

## What the prepayment covers, and what it does not

The prepayment covers the rental days, the statutory charges and the protection products bought in advance,
and never the deposit hold, which is authorised at collection and released at return.

## Where the card is declined

Where the card is declined the rental stays merely booked and is released; a rental is never confirmed
against an unpaid prepayment.

## Currency

A prepaid rental is charged in the currency the supplier publishes, and a conversion the renter elects
carries the class's markup.

## The deposit hold

The deposit hold is the class's own amount, is never treated as a payment, and is released within the
supplier's own banking time after the vehicle is returned undamaged.

## Where the renter later cancels

Where the renter later cancels, the prepayment is the money the cancellation charge is withheld from.

## Basis Q and A

**Is the deposit part of what was paid in advance?** No. The prepayment and the deposit hold are separate
amounts taken at different moments and for different purposes: the prepayment is taken at confirmation and
is money paid, while the deposit is authorised at collection and is a hold.

**What is taken at booking on a class that does not require prepayment?** Nothing until the counter. Such a
class publishes a share of nothing, and the vehicle is paid for at collection.

**Does a conversion markup attach to the deposit?** The markup is carried by a conversion the renter elects
on a prepaid rental. The deposit hold is not a payment, and the class's published markup is a term of the
money taken in advance.
